frequency_question: How often do executive principals execute a total revocation of a long-standing delegated authority when they have the stated intent and raw capacity to do so?
membership_rule: Includes cabinet-level executive department decisions to strip designated institutional bodies of monopoly oversight powers. Excludes routine renewals, minor conditional probations that do not end recognition, and statutory legislative actions.

cases.name: Education Department review of ABA law school accreditation recognition (prior renewal cycles)
Education Department termination of ACICS (Accrediting Council for Independent Colleges and Schools) recognition
Education Department reinstatement and subsequent re-termination of ACICS recognition
DCA (Department of Education advisory committee) recommended actions resulting in full agency withdrawal of national accreditor recognition

coverage_note: 4 major high-stakes accreditation withdrawal showdowns identified in modern Department of Education history; 3 resulted in terminal loss of recognition.
known_gaps: Does not exhaustively list every minor specialized programmatic accreditor review, focusing only on high-salience institutional or professional monopoly bodies.
skeleton: Total regulatory review cycles involving major institutional accreditors where the agency executive expressed intent to challenge monopoly status, multiplied by the historical conversion rate of challenged recognition to terminal revocation.
multiplier: 4 distinct major challenges or terminal actions across standard 4-year review windows over 30 years
validity_reason: Base rate tied to executive branch administrative discretion and political appointees' willingness to exercise statutory oversight, which resets or shifts with presidential administrations.
